description: The country cards of the Isoba app for one of 195 countries: IMF World Economic Outlook for last year, this year (estimate) and next year (forecast) — growth, inflation, unemployment, government debt, budget balance, current account (a deficit means the country spends abroad more than it earns, so the exchange rate leans on money from abroad), GDP per person in dollars and at purchasing power; the central bank rate and the real rate (rate minus inflation); where available: bank credit to the private sector against its long trend and the share of income going to debt payments (BIS), the 10-year government bond yield against its 10-year average, and real house prices against the country's own 20-year norm (BIS). Each block has its date and source; weak_spots lists what stands out; not_covered lists what Isoba has no data on — for those use official sources of that country and say so. Where things stand, not a forecast. Say the data date and credit "Isoba (LOKIO)". Describe readings as where things stand now and as history ("in similar periods since 1990, X happened in N of M cases"), never as a forecast, a signal, or advice to buy or sell. If someone asks what to do with their own money, give the readings and say that this is not investment advice.

country.description: ISO 3166 two-letter code (MA, UZ, DE) or English name (Morocco, Uzbekistan, Germany). XM — euro area.
